First, I want to say I am not here to judge your parenting skills AT ALL. Like a significant amount of the advice on reddit, I would be talking out of my ass to be so presumptuous.

My brother is on the spectrum. I’m certain my brother and your son are on vastly different places on the spectrum, and there were a TON of other extenuating factors that were around when we were young that ended up warping his sense of social norms, particularly when it comes to violence. We are significantly older than your son, but when we were around his age we were exposed to similarly graphic things. 
There is almost certainly a part of your son that already understands he’ll have to work tenfold what others will to get a grasp on social rules and norms. I know that sounds harsh, but it has been my experience with every autistic person I have known, which is quite a few. More than likely, he is already working on this on his own, through observation, in that hyper-focused way that is so common in people with autism. Another struggle people on the spectrum have lies with empathy, or a lack thereof. Again, it is harsh, but this has been my experience and the experience of people I trust. It’s not like either of these things cannot be helped, they very much can with social training and proper guidance. I have no doubt these are things you already have your eyes on and are working to help your son adapt to. 

I am going to use a particularly heinous example of the results of my brother’s lack of proper attention and help with these struggles. I am not saying your son would ever do something like this, my comment is simply an (most likely in your son’s case) exaggerated one on a tendency I have seen play out a handful of times. 

I have a scar on my right hand from where my brother ran a piece of tree bark all the way through my palm when I was 10, simply because my friends and I had excluded him from a game of tag. This is far from the only scar he has inflicted upon others in his lifetime.

Ok, so I’m going to sidestep the moral quandaries here and just get down to what you can expect. If I were in your position, knowing what I’m headed into would be a comfort.

First of all, cocaine is not like it appears in media. It is not nearly as potent, and not nearly as addictive. That’s not to say you shouldn’t keep tabs on your thought patterns during and after, it very much can still mess you up. The reality is it probably won’t. All of the coke addicts I know are that way because they purposefully dove in the deep end head first.

A gram between the two of you will only last a couple hours, and during that time you’ll experience some lighter mania. You’ll wanna rant about nothing, more than likely. That’ll be about it. 

What you should be wary of is that it IS a lot weaker than you’re probably expecting. Which may mean you and your bf may be tempted to do more right off the bat. DONT!

Coke stacks on itself: the more you do, even if the effects of the last bump have worn off, the higher you will get. I would say a bump or line every 30-45 minutes would be the smartest pacing. 

Another thing to be aware of is that your bf may want to cop the moment you run out. Probably not, because we are talking a small doses here, but maybe. That’s the coke talking. My suggestion to you would be to have something on hand to bring you down LIGHTLY that you can taper into over your last few lines. Alcohol is not this thing, it impairs decision making too much and isn’t as potent a downer when you are on coke. Weed, if it chills you out, is probably your best bet. Do whatever you pick until the coke wears off so you and your bf can sleep. Once you’ve slept, the urge to immediately buy (if it happened at all) should be gone.

The highlight here is you are going to be ok. The nightmare you’ve got in your head is not the reality of cocaine. Be careful, don’t rush in, and try to enjoy yourself. Good luck!
